2nd Boon: This Boon can only be activated for the Player who started the Duel going second.

A-Switch: The attaching Ability is activated or benefit gained when this Phantom is Switched into Attack Position.

Any Ability Damage is first dealt to Ability Protection.
The Ability Protection stops damage equal to the attaching amount.

Unless this Ability is Negated.

When active or applied to a Card, it is treated as if it does not have any Ability.

Accumulative Stats: Both of the Card's current Attack and Health Stats combined.
Adaptation: You can activate this Ability once to then select one of the listed Abilities to be activated.

When a Roll Ability has an Advantage Roll you can roll an additional Dice and choose which Roll to use.
Roll Advantage can be stacked, rolling more dice with each one.

If an Ability involves multiple Dice results, you select which dice to use as your results based on how many Advantage Rolls you have.

You can add this Card to your hand from the AL, besides the turn it is sent to the AL, by meeting the attaching Condition or paying the attaching Cost.

Allyless: Control no Ally Phantom or Support Cards on your Side of the field.
Alt Condition:
Another Condition that can be met instead of the primary Condition.
That could potentially have an Alternate Ability.
AP:
AP stands for Ability Point(s).

Cards come into play with a certain number of AP.
Being the Number listed next to the first AP (prior to the AP Abilities).

Any Ability with AP before it cost AP to Activate.
The Number attached to the AP is how many AP that Ability Costs to Activate.
If it has no number by the AP then it only Costs 1 AP to Activate.

Each individual AP Ability, like any other Ability, can only be activated Once per Turn.

Phantom AP by default refreshes back to their Ability AP Number at the start of each new Turn.
If the Phantom’s listed AP Number has “Once Per Round” attached to it then they only refresh at the start of a new Round.
And if it instead says “Once per Summon” they only refresh when newly Summoned.

Spirit and Counter Cards do not regain AP. (Unless otherwise specified).
If Spirit/Counter Cards use all their AP they are sent to the AL.
Armor:
Armor functions similar to Health.
When a Phantom takes Damage it is first dealt to its Armor.
Armor and Health are two separate Stats.
If an Ability takes away more Armor than a Phantom has, this has no effect on its Health.
If a Phantom loses all its Health while it still has Armor, it still has a Break Applied to it.
Asleep:
Countdown Counters are applied for and taken off for the Turns.

Sleep is no longer Applied after the Countdown Ends or if the Asleep Phantom takes Damage.
If a Phantom has both Tired and Sleep Applied to them, then Tired will always Apply first and Sleep will be applied after Tired has ended.

Charmer:
This card can Spend its Attack to Targeted Charm a Card.
Add a Charm Counter the Phantom.
While a Phantom has any Charm Counters they have Charm and Charmed Applied to them.
A Phantom loses a Charm Counter at the end of each Turn.
Apply the following Abilities based on the number of Charm Counters on this Phantom.


1: Cannot Initiate an Attack.
2: Cannot Deal Battle Damage.
3: The Player who does not control this card, on their turn, can have this Phantom Initiate an Attack and choose the Target.


If this Status Effect is Cured or Negated remove all Charm Counters.

Cursed: The card will have an Ability applied to it at a later point or after a Condition is met.

Discarded: Send the card to the After Life.

When only one Player has an Environment in play, both Fields and Players are in the Environment Range.

Evolution:
Evolution Summoning is a Special Summoning Method.

Evolution Phantoms can be Evolution Summoned from the Hand or Extra Deck.
Using the required listed Materials to perform the Summon with.

Materials must be lower Level than the Evolution Phantom.
Some Evolution Phantoms will have additional costs and conditions for an Evolution Summon.

Evolution Summoning can be performed on your turn as a Universal Mechanic, when all Requirements are met and the SP cost can be paid.

When performing an Evolution Summon, using an Ally Phantom on the field as Material, that Phantom’s SP Value counts towards the Evolution Phantom’s SP Cost.

An Evolution Summons cost is reduced by the Field Value of any on Field Phantoms used.

Materials used are stacked up and placed under the Evolution Phantom, becoming an Evolutionary Line.
These Materials stay on the field, until the Evolution Phantom leaves the Field. Whereby they are sent to the AL.

When a Phantom that already has Materials / an Evolutionary Line is used to perform an Evolution Summon, that Phantom and its Materials are added to a new Evolutionary Line.

Some Evolution Summons might only be possible to perform using an Ability.
Some Abilities will let you use Material not on your field. But you must pay the full cost of the Evolution Phantom if you Summon it this way.
Evolution Summoning:
A Special Summoning Method.
When performing an Evolution Summon, you need an Evolution Card.
First you activate the Evolve Ability, paying whatever the attaching cost is.
Once the cost has been successfully paid, the Evolution Summon is performed.
The Phantom being Summoned must meet the conditions attached to the Evolution keyword.

Any Cards used as part of the Evolution Summon immediately become Material.
The Phantom being Evolution Summoned can be Summoned to any available and valid Slot.
(Phantom(s) that have become Material are no longer taking up any Slot. They are not on the field but have not left the field either).

The Material is placed under the Summoned Phantom.
The Material becomes a part of that Phantom’s Evolutionary Line.
If a Phantom with an Evolutionary Line is used to perform another Evolution Summon, that Phantom and its Material become the newly Summoned Phantom’s Evolutionary Line.

The Evolution Summoned Phantom’s SP Value becomes the combined total of the Materials’ on Field SP Value.
Evolve: The cost of Activating this card's Evolution Ability.
Excavate:
Look at a certain number of cards from the top of your deck.
Usually to Draw a chosen card.
Excavate Limit: You can only Activate one Ability with Excavate Limit per turn.

Fell: Send a card to the Bottom of the Player’s Main Deck.

Finale: This Ability can only be activated after all other Conditions / Abilities have been successfully met/activated.

Fragile: After this card Battles, it has a Break applied to it.

Freezer: This Phantom Applies Freeze to any Phantom it Battles, for the number of Attaching Turns.
Frozen:
Frozen Phantoms cannot Initiate an Attack.
While a Phantom has Frozen Applied to them, it takes an additional 100 Damage in Battle multiplied by their Original level.
Fusion:
Fusion Summoning is a Special Summoning Method.

A Fusion Summon can be performed in a variety of ways.

Such as with two (or more) Face up Phantoms that are the same Level. You can use them as Material to Fusion Summon a Fusion Phantom that’s Level is the combined total of all Materials used.
Materials must add up to exactly the Level of the Fusion Phantom.
The Fusion Phantoms Material requirements must be met.


Materials used are stacked up and placed under the Fusion Phantom.
They remain on the field until the Fusion Phantom leaves the Field.
If the Fusion Phantom Breaks, so do the Materials.
If the Fusion Phantom is Unsummoned / Bounced / Removed so are the Materials.

When Fusion Summoned, a Fusion Phantom’s SP Value becomes the combined total of the on Field SP Value of the Materials used.


An Ability can be used to perform a Fusion Summon using Materials not on the Field.

Some Abilities can allow Phantoms of different Levels to be used as Material.
So long as the total combined Level and Materials matches the Fusion Phantoms requirements.

Search Limit: You can only Activate one Search Limit Ability per turn.
Searcher: On Summon: Search for a Card that meets the attaching criteria.
Secretly Search: Search for a card without having to reveal it to your opponent.
Self Aura: The attaching Ability is continuously being applied to this Card.
Self Search: Search a Copy of this Card.
Set Shadow Swap:
Set an eligible Target, from your Hand, Extra Deck, or move one that is already Set.
By first moving this card to where that Set Card will be coming from. (Hand or Extra Deck).
If another Set Card is selected, Swap the Slots of the two Cards.
Shadow Realm Ability: This Ability can only be activated while this Card is in the Shadow Realm.
Shadow Step:
If this card is Targeted, you can Banish this card and Dodge.

At the next Turn Start, Unbanish this card.
All damage and conditions on this card are still applied to it.

Once per card summon.
Shadow Swap:
You can Special Summon a Phantom of ≤ SP. It can be Special Summoned from your Hand, Extra Deck, or from having been Set as a Counter Form or Spirit Form.
This Phantom can be Special Summoned Face Down without revealing what it is.
This activating Phantom is first sent to the Hand, Extra Deck, or is Set based on where the Special Summoned Phantom is being Summoned from.
Sharpness: Player Battle Damage dealt by this card is increased by the Attaching Amount.
Shielded:
The first damage this card would take is negated.
This only applied once per Shielded application. Often meaning once per summon.
Slash: When this Phantom Initiates Battle – Deal the listed Damage to any Phantoms on both sides of the Defending Phantom.
Sleep:
When a Phantom has Sleep Applied to them are Asleep, for the listed number of Turns.
Countdown Counters are applied for and taken off for the Turns.
While Asleep Phantoms are unable to Initiate an Attack, Deal Battle Damage, or Activate an Ability.
Sleep is no longer Applied after the Countdown Ends or if the Asleep Phantom takes Damage.
If a Phantom has both Tired and Sleep Applied to them, then Tired will always Apply first and Sleep will be applied after Tired has ended.
Slow: This Ability is one Speed slower than normal.
Slow Start: This Phantom is unable to Attack the turn it is Summoned.
Solo: You can only play one copy of this card in any of your Decks.
Soul Bound: A Copy of this card always starts in your opening Mulligan.
Soul Break: When this Card Successfully Breaks another Card all of that Card's Copies in the Opponent's Hand or Decks have a Break applied to them as well.
Special Exchange:
A Special Exchange does not cost SP.
Exchange a Phantom from your hand, placing it into your Extra Deck, and adding an Extra Deck card back to your hand.
This counts as an Extra Deck Exchange.
Special Extra Deck Extract: Add an Extra Deck card to your hand.
Special Extract:
Add an Extra Deck card to your hand.
This counts as an Extra Deck Extract.
Special Resurrect:
Special Summon a Phantom from your AL.
This counts as a Resurrect Summon.


Some Resurrect Abilities may allow you to use the Enemy After Life.
Such as if it states something like "any".
Special Ritual Summon:
You can activate a Ritual Summon Ability in hand.
After meeting the attaching conditions/requirements you can Special Summon the Phantom.
Special Swap:
This keyword acts as a Swap while in hand. This Keyword acts like Swap while on the field.

But gains an Additional Field Ability:

Select a Phantom that meets the listed requirements from your Hand or Extra Deck. Place this Activating Phantom where the Selected Phantom is and then Special Summon that Phantom.
Spin: Shuffle a card randomly into the Player’s Main Deck.
Spirit Form:
You can play this Card as if it was a Spirit to use the Attaching Ability.
This Card is treated as a Spirit Card while using Spirit Form.
This Card can be placed face down the same as a Spirit Card.
Its Activation and Resolution are the same as a Spirit and it is sent to the AL after using its Ability.
Spiritless: Control no Ally Spirit Cards on your side of the Field.
SR Return:
You can add this Card to your hand from the Shadow Realm, besides the turn it is sent to the Shadow Realm, by meeting the attaching Condition or paying the attaching Cost.
Shadow Realm Return can only be used Once per turn per Card.
Stab: Deal additional Summoner Battle Damage equal to the attaching amount.
Stance Switch: Switch the Battle Position of a Phantom.
Stat Swap: Swap the current Attack and Health of a Phantom.
Static:
Phantoms that have Static Applied to them have Delayed Attack.
The Enemy Phantom Deals their Attack Damage first in Battle.
Static Shocker: This Phantom Applies Static to any Phantom it Damages.
Stats: Both the Attack and Health of a Phantom.
Status Effect:
Various Keywords that are Applied to Phantoms with varying Abilities.
Including: Burn, Poison, Static, Paralysis, Freeze (Frozen), Tired, Sleep (Asleep).
Stealth:
This card cannot be Targeted by the opponent until it Activates an Ability or declares an Attack.
Reveal negates Stealth.
Stories:
This Ability costs the listed number as Story Line Counters to activate.
Is treated as a Story Ability.
Story Card:
Any Card with a Story Inspiration is a Story Card.

When a attaching Story Inspiration Condition is met this "Story Card" Gains +1 Story Counter (SC).

A SC Ability Costs 1+ SC to activate.

Any Chapters (Ch.) must be activated in order.
Their SC Cost equals their Ch.#.

SC / Ch. Abilities are Once per Duel.
Once all Abilities have been used, AL Send the Card.

Story Cards that share the same Name -- also share Story Counters and Chapter Progress.
Multiple copies in play do not get multiple Inspirations.
Newly Played Story Cards, gain previous held SC.

SC / Ch. Abilities are both treated as Story Abilities.
Story Finale:
This Ability can only be activated after all other Story Abilities have been activated.
This is treated as both a Story and Finale Ability.
Story Inspiration:
Any Card with a Story Inspiration is a Story Card.

When a attaching Story Inspiration Condition is met this "Story Card" Gains +1 Story Counter (SC).

Story Line:
Chapter (Ch.) Abilities must be used in order.

They Cost SC equal to their Ch.#.

Ch. Abilities are treated as Story Abilities and are Once per Duel.
Strength: This Phantom does additional Damage in Battle by the Attaching amount.
Strike: Direct Attacks deal additional Damage to the Player equal to the attaching amount.
Sturdy:
The first time this Phantom would Break, that Break is Negated.
If this happens as a result of the Phantom losing all its Health, it stays on zero health and the Zero Health Rules apply.
Summon Inspire: Whenever a Phantom is Summoned, gain the attaching Ability or benefit.
Summon Overdrive: SP on the next turn is automatically paid out equal to the attaching amount.
Summoner Battle Damage: The Player takes Summoner Damage in Battle for all excess Attack beyond their Phantom's Health.
Summoner Damage: Any damage that is applied to the Summoner as a result of Attacks or Battle.
Super Breaker: Whenever this card Battles with another card, after the Battle resolves, that card has a Break applied to it.
Super Draw Duel Limit: You can only Activate a single Draw Ability with Super Draw Ability once per Duel.
Supportless: Control no Ally Support Cards on your side of the Field.
Suppress:
A card that has been Suppressed has its Abilities turned off for the turn.
If it's Ability is already Activated and on the Line -- that Ability will still happen.
Swap:
Hand Ability: Select a Phantom that meets the listed requirements from your Extra Deck. Swap the two Phantoms.

Field Ability:
Select an Ally Phantom that meets the requirements. Swap their Field Slot positions.
Attacks Declared towards a swapped Phantom are aimed at the Phantom now in its place.
Swift Strike:
This Ability activates whenever this Phantom Battles. Deal this Phantom's Attack to the Battling Phantom prior to Battle Initializing.
If the other Phantom survives then Battle progresses as normal.
Switch Out: Once per Turn: Add this card back to hand and Special Summon a Phantom of equal or less SP and that meets the listed requirements.
Synthesis:
Synthesis Summoning is a Special Summoning Method.

Synthesis Phantoms can be Synthesis Summoned from the Hand or Extra Deck.
Using the required listed Materials to perform the Summon with.

Synthesis Summoning can be performed on your turn as a Universal Mechanic if you have a Synthesis Phantom with valid Materials on the Field. Or a Synthesis Summon Ability.

You can use any number of Materials to perform a Synthesis Summon. Each card used as a Material Reduces the SP Value of the Synthesis Card.

A Synthesis Summons cost is reduced by the Field Value of any on Field Phantoms used.

Spend any remaining needed SP to perform the Synthesis summon beyond what the Material used covers.
If you do not have enough SP you cannot perform a Synthesis Summon. Except for if it is a Special Summon.

Materials used are stacked up and placed under the Synthesis Phantom.
These Materials stay on the field, as Synthesis Materials, until the Synthesis Phantom leaves the Field.

An Ability can be used to perform a Synthesis Summon using Materials not on the Field.
Target: This card Targets a Card for the ability to be applied to.
Targeted: This card Targets a Card for the ability to be applied to.
Targeted Dodge Roll: Can be activated in response to this card or it’s Card Slot being Targeted. This card must move to an available adjacent card Slot for this Ability to be activated. Dodge the Targeted Action.
Targeted Reveal: Target a card on the field to Reveal.
Targeting Taunter:
Ally Cards without Taunter cannot be Targeted while a Targeting Taunter Phantom is Face Up on the Field.
If there is an Attaching condition, then only the Cards that meet that condition are protected by Taunter.
Taunter:
Ally Cards without Taunter cannot be Targeted for an Attack while a Taunter Phantom is Face Up on the Field.
If there is an Attaching condition, then only the Cards that meet that condition are protected by Taunter.
Threat:
The Counter can only be turned up at the start of the turn to become active.

Its Condition being met has the card's Ability automatically go off.

If its Condition is not met by the end of the turn it was activated this card is sent to the AL.
Timer:
Add a Counter to this card based on the attaching Ability at the end of each turn.
Such as adding 1 Turn Counter at the end of each turn.
Tired:
While Tired Phantoms are unable to Initiate an Attack.
Tired is no longer Applied after the Countdown Ends or if the Tired Phantom takes Damage.
If a Phantom has both Tired and Sleep Applied to them, then Tired will always Apply first and Sleep will be applied after Tired has ended.
Token:
A card treated as a Phantom.
If details are not given for a token, it is to be treated as a Level 0 Phantom without an Ability, 0-Stats, and no Archetype.
Transformation:
Perform a Transformation Summon by:
Special Summoning a Phantom that meets the Attaching Conditions.
Paying any difference in SP Value. (If that Phantom costs more SP than the Transforming Phantom's current SP Value).

Place the Special Summoned Phantom on top of the Transforming Phantom.
This creates an Evolutionary Line.
Further Transformation or Evolution Summons are added on top of this Evolutionary Line.

A Transformation Summon counts as an Evolution Summon.
Unequip: Send a Card currently Equipped to this one to the AL.
Unsummon:
Send a Phantom you control to the AL and Gain their current Summoning Points back.
You can freely Unsummon on your Turn as a Game Action.
You cannot Unsummon a card the turn it has Battled.
A Phantom cannot be Unsummoned by Abilities when Attacked or during Battle.
Victory Boon: When this Phantom Defeats another Phantom in Battle, activate the attaching Ability.
Vulnerability: This Phantom receives additional damage equal to the attaching Damage amount every time that it receives Damage.
Weakness: This Phantom deals less Damage in Battle by the Attaching amount.
Xerox:
Xerox Summoning is a Special Summoning Method.

You can Initiate a Xerox Summon when you have a Xerox Phantom in your hand or Extra Deck. As long as you have the correct materials.

Phantoms used as Xerox Materials must be the same level as the Xerox Phantom.
They also must contain at least one shared Archetype with the Xerox Phantom.

When performing a Xerox Summon, you Create a Copy of the Xerox Phantom, which is now considered a Xerox Copy.
Materials used are stacked up and placed under the Xerox Copy.
These Materials stay on the field, and are considered Ink Material, until the Xerox Copy leaves the Field.

You can detach Ink Material, sending them to the AL, when performing certain Xerox Phantom Abilities.

When a Xerox Copy has no material left, at the end of a turn, it Breaks.
When a Xerox Copy Breaks or otherwise leaves the field it is removed from play. And its Materials go to the AL.

Xerox Phantoms cannot be Summoned through other Summoning Methods besides Xerox Summoning.
